extracted.intended_audience: U.S.-based small business concerns (SBCs) preparing NIH/CDC SBIR grant applications that propose clinical trials
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting NIH/CDC SBIR Phase I/II (and related) grant applications under NOFO PA-24-246 that must propose clinical trials, including Fast-Track, Direct-to-Phase-II, and Phase IIB variants and commercialization documentation. Covers eligibility, phase-specific objectives, and commercialization/third-party funding expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — U.S. small business concern (SBC) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: This NOFO invites eligible United States small business concerns (SBCs) to submit SBIR Phase I, Phase II, Direct to Phase II (NIH Only), Fast-Track (NIH only), and Phase IIB (NIH only) grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be US-owned and operated small businesses that meet SBIR program eligibility rules. STTR applicants should submit to the STTR-specific NOFOs (PA-24-247 or PA-24-248). Use the official agency solicitation link to confirm current rules and required forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I objective — establish technical merit and feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The main objective in SBIR and STTR Phase I is to establish the technical merit and feasibility of the proposed research and development efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase I proposals should focus on demonstrating proof of concept/feasibility sufficient to justify advancement to Phase II. Investigators proposing NIH-defined clinical trials may refer to Research Methods Resources for study design and statistical methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II objective — advance toward commercialization
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR and STTR Phase II continues the R&D efforts to advance the technology toward ultimate commercialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the conclusion of Phase II it is expected the small business will fully commercialize their product or technology using non-SBIR/STTR funds (federal or non-federal). Phase II proposals should demonstrate a clear path toward market and further development beyond feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single Phase II award per Phase I-supported project
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one Phase II application may be awarded for a specific project supported by a Phase I award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small businesses eligible to submit Phase II applications for projects supported with a Phase I award are expected to submit the regular Phase II application as a 'Renewal' application based on the awarded Phase I project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fast-Track option — combined Phase I and Phase II submission and review (NIH only)
rubrics_metrics.description: An NIH SBIR Fast-Track incorporates a submission and review process in which both Phase I and Phase II applications are submitted and reviewed together as one application to reduce or eliminate the funding gap between phases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Fast-Track only when you have a coherent plan for both phases and can justify combined review to accelerate progress. Fast-Track is NIH-only; follow NIH-specific instructions in the NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct to Phase II eligibility and submission rules (NIH only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct to Phase II is for small businesses that have already demonstrated scientific and technical merit and feasibility but have not received a Phase I SBIR or STTR for that project. NIH will accept Direct to Phase II applications regardless of the funding source for the proof-of-principle work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct to Phase II awards should be submitted as 'New' applications and not as continuations ('Renewal') of Phase I SBIR or STTR projects. Provide documentation of prior proof-of-principle and justify bypassing Phase I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase IIB purpose and additional funding criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase IIB provides additional funding for Phase II SBIR/STTR projects that require considerable financing beyond the SBIR/STTR Phase II to achieve commercialization, typically for projects requiring extraordinary time and effort (e.g., regulatory approval, complex instrumentation, clinical research tools, behavioral interventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH ICs may allow submission of Phase IIB applications; check IC-specific topics and targeted funding opportunities for details and any extra requirements (e.g., letter of intent). Follow IC instructions where Phase IIB is accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial potential is a strong review/funding consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial potential (the probability that an application will result in a commercial product) will be strongly considered in review and making funding decisions for Phase IIB and other relevant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should clearly articulate market opportunity, commercialization strategy, and milestones that demonstrate a realistic path to commercialization. Strong commercial potential increases competitiveness for funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation and encouragement to secure substantial independent third‑party investor funding
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant's ability to secure substantial independent third-party investor funds will help validate the commercial potential of the proposed Phase IIB project. Applicants are encouraged to secure substantial independent third-party investor funds (i.e., third-party funds that equal or exceed the requested NIH funds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of third-party investors include another company, venture capital, angel investors, foundations, universities, research institutions, or state/local government. Provide details of investor commitments or plans in the application; include letters of support if funding has already been secured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization plan requirement for Phase IIB applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide a commercialization plan that describes the long-term commercialization strategy and details of any independent third-party investor funding that has already been secured or will be provided during the Phase IIB project period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commercialization plan should include timelines, milestones, market analysis, regulatory strategy (if applicable), financing plan, and letters of support from third‑party investors where appropriate. The presence of such documentation strengthens an application's commercial viability claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial requirement for this Parent NOFO
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications submitted to this Parent Notice of Funding Opportunity must propose clinical trial(s). SBIR applications that do not propose clinical trial(s) should be submitted to PA-24-245.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the application includes an appropriately designed clinical trial protocol, relevant regulatory considerations, and adherence to NIH clinical trial policies. Use available NIH Research Methods Resources for design and statistical guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application assignment and requesting an awarding component
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are not required to identify a potential awarding component prior to submission but may request one on the Assignment Request Form. CSR will assign applications to the most appropriate Agency and Institute/Center based on their mission and the science proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a preferred Institute/Center, indicate it on the Assignment Request Form. Familiarize yourself with the missions of NIH ICs to support an informed assignment request; CSR makes final assignment decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted application types under this NOFO
rubrics_metrics.description: This NOFO accepts SBIR Phase I, Phase II, Direct to Phase II (NIH only), Fast-Track (NIH only), and Phase IIB (NIH only) grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the correct application mechanism for your project and follow the specific instructions and forms for that mechanism in the official solicitation. For STTR-specific pathways, submit to the STTR NOFOs referenced (PA-24-247 or PA-24-248).
